newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada lets some shippers use 1997/98 lumber quota.
newsitem.headline: Canada lets some shippers use 1997/98 lumber quota.

text.p: Canada will allow small lumber producers, who have exceeded their limits for softwood lumber shipments to the United States, to borrow up to 20 percent of their quotas for next year, a source familiar with the situation said on Tuesday.

"They've come up with a scheme to allow small producers, those with sales of under 50 million board feet (a year), to borrow up to 20 percent of next year's quota. Next year only," the source told Reuters.

Canadian lumber producers received their annual export quotas from the government on October 31 but on Monday it became clear that some companies had already reached or were close to reaching their annual allocations. Company quotas are confidential and it is up to the companies to reveal what they are.

Under a five-year agreement between Canada and the United States which became effective on April 1, Canadian lumber shipments which exceed 14.7 billion board feet a year, or 4.226 billion board feet quarterly, are subject to export fees.
Lumber companies who exceed their quotas face fees of US$50 for every 1,000 board feet on the first 650 million board feet and US$100 for every 1,000 board feet on any shipments exceeding that.
The company quotas are to be reviewed every year for the remaining four years of the agreement.
